implementation_notes: Interfaces are satisfied implicitly, so the interface can be declared in the package that consumes it and the implementation package needs no knowledge of it - the strongest form of the pattern, because the contract lives exactly where the implementation cannot be imported. Producers return concrete types; consumers accept the narrow interface they need, which keeps it one or two methods wide. Declare the interface in the producer only when it is a stable, widely shared contract or a genuine plugin point.
pitfalls: A typed nil inside an interface value is not nil: returning (*T)(nil) where an interface or error is expected produces a silently non-nil value.
Interfaces declared next to the implementation grow to mirror it; keep them at the consumer and as small as the call site allows.
Interface indirection defeats devirtualization in hot loops; measure before abstracting a concrete type that is already fast.
